name: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma

criteria.description: Presence of solitary or multiple yellowish to reddish-brown papules or nodules on the skin
Skin biopsy showing dermal infiltration by histiocytes with Touton giant cells
Onset typically in infancy or early childhood
No evidence of malignant histiocytosis or Langerhans cell histiocytosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cutaneous lesions plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Systemic involvement is rare but should be evaluated if present

pathognomonic.symptomName: Yellowish to reddish-brown cutaneous papules or nodules
searchTerms: yellow to reddish brown skin bumps

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Touton giant cells on histopathology
searchTerms: giant multinucleated cells seen in biopsy
specific large cells in tissue samples

common.symptomName: Lesions predominantly on head, neck, and upper trunk
searchTerms: skin lesions mainly on head and neck
lesions on head, neck, and chest

common.symptomName: Spontaneous regression of skin lesions over months to years
searchTerms: skin lesions that disappear over time
small lumps on colored part of eye

occasional.notes: Rare but possible in disseminated cases
searchTerms: involvement of liver, lungs, and brain

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS involvement
searchTerms: neurological symptoms from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to central nervous system disease
brain or spinal cord related neurological signs
fever related to whole body condition

laboratory: Normal blood counts; occasional mild leukocytosis if systemic involvement
Histopathology showing dermal histiocytic infiltration with Touton giant cells
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI may reveal systemic lesions if present
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations associated
other: Spontaneous regression of lesions without treatment in most cases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Birbeck granules on electron microscopy
Lesions typically lack Touton giant cells

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or ulcerating skin lesions
Systemic symptoms such as persistent fever or weight loss
references: Haroche J, et al. Juvenile xanthogranuloma: clinical and pathological features. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2018.
Klein CE, et al. Juvenile xanthogranuloma: a review of clinical and histopathologic features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019.
